headline: Analytic and evaluation choices can flip reported biological conclusions
label: Evaluation Choice Robustness Audits
summary: Recent preprints show that rich-club, survival, and benchmark conclusions shift with analysis choices, motivating explicit robustness testing.
synthesis: The dominant thread across these preprints is that reported biological effects depend on analysis and evaluation choices. A survival-analysis reanalysis of public striatal optogenetics seizure data applies log-rank, Cox, permutation, and leave-one-out checks to test the robustness of ChR2 timing effects. In Alzheimer's EEG, rich-club group differences are created or erased by null network construction and hub re-identification. A proteomic co-abundance benchmark finds that method rankings shift with evaluation depth and that no method dominates. Stroke efferocytosis scoring against expression-matched nulls, and a conditioned sequence model that predicts interferon-beta responses but not stimulus-dependent genetic effects, follow the same emphasis on explicit testing. This framing is dominant rather than universal across the set. What is new is the explicit demonstration that identical data can support different conclusions under alternative analytic choices.
